operations.description: List the conversations the token can see, one page per call of at most limit (1 to 1000); each later call sends the previous page's response_metadata.next_cursor as cursor, and the walk ends on a page whose next_cursor is empty. Slack reports a failed read as status 200 with ok false

Read one conversation's messages, newest first, one page per call, optionally within oldest and latest (Slack ts); each later call sends the previous page's response_metadata.next_cursor as cursor, and the walk ends on a page whose next_cursor is empty. Slack reports a failed read as status 200 with ok false

Read one thread, the parent message identified by channel and ts followed by its replies, one page per call, optionally within oldest and latest (Slack ts); each later call sends the previous page's response_metadata.next_cursor as cursor, and the walk ends on a page whose next_cursor is empty. Slack reports a failed read as status 200 with ok false

List the workspace's users, one page per call; each later call sends the previous page's response_metadata.next_cursor as cursor, and the walk ends on a page whose next_cursor is empty. Send limit: without it Slack tries to answer the whole list at once. Slack reports a failed read as status 200 with ok false

Read the token's workspace under team: its id, name and domain; the optional team parameter names another workspace the token sees through a shared channel. Slack reports a failed read as status 200 with ok false

List the workspace's custom emoji in one call, not paged. The pinned document states no member of the answer beyond ok; Slack's answer is returned as it came. Slack reports a failed read as status 200 with ok false
Read who the connection's token is: user_id, user, team_id, team and url, plus bot_id for a bot token. Slack reports a token it does not accept as status 200 with ok false

List the files the token can see under files, each with its id, name, filetype, mimetype, size and url_private, optionally narrowed by channel, user, types and ts_from and ts_to (Slack ts); one page per call of count files, page counting from 1, each answer with paging.page and paging.total, and paging.pages where Slack states it; the walk ends on the page numbered paging.pages, or on one that lists no file. Needs files:read. Slack reports a failed read as status 200 with ok false
Read one file by its id under file: its name, filetype, mimetype, size and url_private, which file.download reads. Needs files:read. Slack reports a failed read as status 200 with ok false

Read a file's content from its url_private or url_private_download, as files.info and files.list give it: an https URL on files.slack.com under /files-pri/, sent with the connection's token. Answers the bytes in base64 with their media_type, length and sha256, refused above 2 MiB

Post one message, body.text, to the conversation body.channel: a channel id, or the direct message conversations.open answers; body.thread_ts makes it a reply in that thread, body.mrkdwn false turns Slack markup off and body.unfurl_links true unfurls text links. Answers channel, ts (the message's address) and message. Needs chat:write, and the bot in the channel. Nothing exists to compare before a create, so the same input approved and sent again posts a second message. The token's auth.test is read first and must answer ok true, or nothing is sent. Slack refuses a post (channel_not_found, not_in_channel, missing_scope) as status 200 with ok false; the answer must carry ok true to be applied, so such a refusal is outcome_unknown, never applied, and Slack's error string is not returned

Open, or resume, the direct message with the users body.users names: one user id for a direct message, or a comma-separated list of user ids for a multi-person one; body.return_im true asks for the whole conversation. Answers channel.id, the conversation chat.postMessage then names as channel. Needs im:write, and mpim:write for a multi-person conversation. The token's auth.test is read first and must answer ok true, or nothing is sent. Slack refuses (user_not_found, missing_scope) as status 200 with ok false; the answer must carry ok true to be applied, so such a refusal is outcome_unknown, never applied, and Slack's error string is not returned
